name: Switzerland
summary: Four-pillar policy (prevention, therapy, harm reduction, enforcement). Adults: up to 10 g cannabis is not punishable and use is a CHF 100 ticket; other drug use is a fined contravention. Drug checking is legal.
callingForHelp: Ambulance (144) staff are bound by medical secrecy and police are not routinely called. Health and social workers need not report drug use (Art. 3c BetmG). No Good Samaritan law.
drugChecking: Legal, organised by cantons and cities: fixed and mobile services, e.g. in Zurich, Bern, Basel, Geneva and Lucerne.

betmvv.title: Narcotics Lists Ordinance (BetmVV-EDI, SR 812.121.11), status 13 March 2026

bvgerDxm.title: Federal Administrative Court: DXM cough medicines not to be sold in drugstores

cannabisBill.title: Hanf-Magazin: National Council committee sends cannabis bill (20.473) back to subcommittee, May 2026

alkg.title: Alcohol Act (AlkG, SR 680), Art. 41: no spirits to under-18s

lmg.title: Food Act (LMG, SR 817.0), Art. 14: no alcohol to under-16s

lsd.note: Prohibited (list d). Use or possession for own use is a contravention punished by a fine (Art. 19a BetmG); supply up to 3 years prison.

mushrooms.note: Hallucinogenic mushrooms (Psilocybe, Panaeolus, Conocybe, Stropharia), truffles included, are prohibited (list d). Own use is fined.

dmt.note: DMT is prohibited (list d), so ayahuasca is illegal too. Own use is fined; supply carries prison.

mescaline.note: Mescaline, peyote and San Pedro (Trichocereus pachanoi) are all listed as prohibited (list d).

dox.note: DOM, DOB and DOC are prohibited (list d); other analogues fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

nbomes.note: 25B-, 25C- and 25I-NBOMe are prohibited (list d); other NBOMes fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other common 2C-x are prohibited (list d); remaining analogues fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are prohibited (list d); other 2C-T-x fall under the generic phenethylamine group (list e).

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and 5-MeO-DiPT are named in list e (controlled like narcotics), which also has a generic tryptamine group.

cannabis.note: Adults: ≤10 g for own use not punishable; use is a CHF 100 ticket. CBD under 1% THC legal. City pilot trials sell to enrolled adults; regulation bill pending.

ketamine.note: Controlled narcotic (list b) used as a prescription medicine. Use or possession without prescription is an offence (fine for own use).

mxe.note: Prohibited (list d); other arylcyclohexylamines fall under a generic group (list e).

dxm.note: Not a controlled narcotic. Cough medicines with DXM are category B since 2019: supplied only by pharmacists or doctors, not drugstores.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic. Supplying it for inhalation is banned under chemicals law (Basel case, final 2024); food/technical sale and possession are legal.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are controlled (list a): own use is fined, supply carries prison. ADHD drugs (methylphenidate etc.) on prescription.

mdma.note: Prohibited (list d). Own use is fined (Art. 19a BetmG); supply up to 3 years, more in serious cases.

cocaine.note: Controlled narcotic. Own use is fined (Art. 19a BetmG); dealing up to 3 years prison, at least 1 year in serious cases.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely in food, drinks and tablets.

alcohol.note: Beer, wine and cider from 16; spirits and alcopops from 18. Cantons may be stricter (e.g. Ticino: 18 for all alcohol).

ghb/gbl.note: GHB and GBL are controlled (list a; GBL exempt only for industrial use); 1,4-BD is in list e. Sodium oxybate is a prescription medicine.

opioids.note: Heroin is prohibited outside heroin-assisted treatment; morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl etc. are prescription-only controlled narcotics.

tramadol.note: Prescription medicine. Ready-to-use tramadol products are exempt from narcotics controls (list b) but still need a prescription.

benzodiazepines.note: Most are controlled prescription medicines (list b); designer benzodiazepines such as flualprazolam are prohibited (list d).

maois.note: Moclobemide and other MAOI drugs need a prescription. Harmala alkaloids/Syrian rue are not listed, but ayahuasca is illegal (DMT).
